  "Measured 4-CN effect: results-ratios.md q02 1.08x, q11 1.46x, q22 1.13x speed-up vs 1.7-2.35x for scan-heavy queries",

 ],

 ],

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run bench-kit TPC-H queries against the FE on 9030 with a /* marker */ so the FE audit log ties QueryId to (query, run).
# usage: run-queries.sh <tag> <tpch_data> <out_dir> <timeout_s> <runs_after_warmup> q01 q02 ...
# writes <out_dir>/runs.csv (query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc) and <out_dir>/<q>.r<i>.out (mysql --batch)
TAG=$1; DATA=$2; OUT=$3; TO=$4; RUNS=$5; shift 5
QD=/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf/experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries
mkdir -p $OUT; echo "query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc" > $OUT/runs.csv
M="mysql --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9030 --user root --batch --connect-timeout=5"
for q in "$@"; do
  sql=$(sed "s#__TPCH_DATA__#$DATA#g" $QD/$q.sql)
  for i in $(seq 0 $RUNS); do
    phase=warm; [ $i = 0 ] && phase=cold
    start=$(date -u +%FT%T.%3N); t0=$(date +%s%N)
    if timeout $TO $M -e "/* $TAG $q r$i */ $sql" > $OUT/$q.r$i.out 2> $OUT/$q.r$i.err; then st=pass; else st=fail; rc=$?; fi
    ms=$(( ($(date +%s%N) - t0) / 1000000 )); rows=$(( $(wc -l < $OUT/$q.r$i.out) - 1 )); [ $rows -lt 0 ] && rows=0
    [ $st = fail ] && [ $ms -ge $((TO*1000 - 500)) ] && st=timeout
    echo "$q,$i,$phase,$st,$ms,$rows,$start" >> $OUT/runs.csv
    echo "$q r$i $phase $st ${ms}ms rows=$rows $( [ $st != pass ] && head -c 160 $OUT/$q.r$i.err | tr '\n' ' ')"
    [ $st != pass ] && break   # a failing run skips the rest of that query (bench.sh semantics)
  done
done

input.reasoning:
Headline holds, mechanism attribution and impact need correction. The measured core is confirmed from the logs and the code: every CN run spends ~190-260 ms before the first fragment runs, and the components are real.

CONFIRMED (measured + source):
- 8 get_file_schema RPCs per query regardless of tables used: QueryAnalyzer.analyzeCTE (QueryAnalyzer.java:360-380) calls processCteRelation for every CTE in the WITH clause; each FILES() reference constructs a fresh TableFunctionTable (QueryAnalyzer.java:2194 -> TableFunctionTable.java:225-240 -> setSchemaForLoadAndQuery :255-264 -> getFileSchema :688-720 -> BackendServiceClient.getFileSchema :712). No cache in FE (grep of SessionVariable/Config/TableFunctionTable for schema cache: none) or CN. FE log confirms 8 HdfsService.listFileMeta lines per run (cn1/cluster.log FE lines 13:12:34.759-34.823). CN reads every footer serially: file_schema.rs:60-97 `for path in rest { parquet_file_schema(path).await? }`; lineitem = 60 files (ls /scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000/lineitem), RPC busy 28.3-29.2 ms + idle 6.4-7.2 ms.
- Deploy is root-first and waits per group before the next; leaves (scans) are in the last groups so the entire deploy is on the critical path before the first scan (cn1 q11.r1: first leaf a92 started 34.9739, 1.4 ms after the group-5 RPC closed at 34.9725; groups 1-4 contained only receivers, which under receiver-first rendezvous cannot run).
- Rendezvous tolerates arrival order: local_exchange.rs push_sender (:142-156) inserts into `sources` via entry().or_default() even when no receiver is registered; take_ready (:248-) returns None until the receiver registers; push_remote_frame (:159-) likewise.
- pre-first-fragment (client start -> first 'fragment run started', from my agent-notes/mfs3_span.py over runs.csv + cluster.log): cn1 q02 r1/r2 195/189, q11 233/227, q15 193/190, q22 199/136; cn4 q02 175/200, q11 262/257, q15 206/211, q22 118/155 ms. Tail after last fragment 2-8 ms.

CONTRADICTED / CORRECTED FROM SOURCE:
1. Wave mechanism is not `threeStageExecutionsToDeploy`. AllAtOnceExecutionSchedule.schedule (AllAtOnceExecutionSchedule.java:130-136) iterates `dag.getFragmentsInTopologicalOrderFromRoot()` (ExecutionDAG.java:195-262, BFS levels of the fragment tree) and calls deployer.createFragmentExecStates + deployFragments ONCE PER LEVEL. On 1 CN each level has a single non-empty stage (Deployer.java:230-256: worker already in deployedWorkerIds -> everything goes to stage 2), so waves == levels. q11 = 9 RPCs in 6 levels (1/1/2/2/2/1), not '8 RPCs in 3 waves'; q02 = 13 in 5 levels (1/7/2/2/2). Collapsing the three stages inside Deployer.deployFragments would not merge levels; the loop to change is AllAtOnceExecutionSchedule.schedule.
2. Inter-level dead time is not FE planning work: it is ~40 ms (measured 38-46, one 28) and occurs ONLY after levels whose replies share a connection (>=2 replies); single-reply levels are followed by the next request within 1-2 ms (cn1 q11.r1 per-RPC: level1 close +118.7 -> next arrival +119.8; level2 close +123.0 -> +124.7; level3 (2 replies) close +143.3 -> +184.5; level4 (2) +200.9 -> +228.8; level5 (2) +231.5 -> +271.6; cn4 q11.r1 gaps 13/46/42/41 with 5-9 RPCs over 4 connections). The CN's accept loop never sets TCP_NODELAY on accepted sockets (brpc.rs:110-130 `Ok((stream, peer)) => connections.spawn(handle_connection(...))`; grep set_nodelay in src/: only prpc_client.rs:170 for outgoing and the nixl test harness) and replies are small frames written per request (prpc.rs:345-356 write_async). That is the Nagle + delayed-ACK signature (2nd small reply held until the FE's delayed ACK of the 1st; FE has nothing to send until the level completes). INFERENCE, medium confidence; verify with `stream.set_nodelay(true)` at brpc.rs:114 or a loopback tcpdump. If right, the deploy critical path for q11 drops from ~116 ms to the ~43 ms of serialized CN handler time (translation 12-18 ms for the bigger fragments; the connection loop brpc.rs:150-190 handles read->call->write sequentially, so a level's RPCs queue behind each other) with no FE change.
3. Proposal (2) 'single deployAsync + wait' is unsafe as written: Deployer.java:247-251 sends stage-2 fragments with emptyDescTable(is_cached=true) and the CN's resolve_descriptor_table (compute_node_service.rs:954-988) returns 'descriptor table cache miss for query' if such a reference is processed before the fragment carrying the table; with all fragments in flight at once over a pooled set of connections (BrpcProxy.java:35-50 shareChannelPool, brpc_connection_pool_size) the ordering is not guaranteed. It needs the FE to send the full desc table on every request or the CN to buffer.
4. An existing knob already covers the 1-CN case: `SET enable_single_node_schedule = true` (SessionVariable.java:3336-3337, default false) -> DefaultCoordinator.maybeChangeScheduler (DefaultCoordinator.java:696-703, needs workerNum==1) -> JobSpec.supportSingleNodeParallelSchedule (JobSpec.java:538-541; FileScanNode is NOT in ScanNode.isConnectorScanNode's list at ScanNode.java:254-258) -> SingleNodeSchedule -> Deployer.deployFragmentsForSingleNode (Deployer.java:363-390) = ONE exec_batch_plan_fragments RPC; the CN implements it (compute_node_service.rs:424-450, translate_batch_attachment :1624-1679, applying common_param.desc_tbl to every instance, so no cache race; unit tests :2169, :2284). Untested on this workload in the campaign. Not available for 4 CNs.
5. Schema RPC: the FE already sends `schema_sample_file_count` (TableFunctionTable.java:631, default DEFAULT_AUTO_DETECT_SAMPLE_FILES = 2 at :114, user-settable via the FILES() property auto_detect_sample_files :128) and the CN deliberately ignores it (file_schema.rs:52-58 'Deliberately stricter than native StarRocks ... reads every file'). Honoring it is a protocol-native alternative to the proposed cache/concurrency (cuts the lineitem call from ~35 ms to ~1 ms), at the cost of the fail-closed whole-set check.
6. The '4 CN 267 ms' is inflated by the harness, not the FE. run-queries.sh:9-14 spawns a new `mysql` process per run; the mysql CLI's `select @@version_comment limit 1` probe is planned by the FE as a UNION_NODE fragment (TPlanNodeType 19, survey/TPlanNodeType.map.txt:20) and deployed to a CN which rejects it ('unsupported plan node TPlanNodeType(19)', FE log 13:12:34.755 / 13:20:06.686), then `select $$` fails to parse. Probe FE time is bimodal: 5-11 ms or 44-50 ms (cn1 8 of 47 probes in the 44-49 tail; cn4 18 of 45); cn4 q11.r1's probe took 46 ms (audit Time=46). Client wall minus FE audit Time: cn1 q02/q11/q15/q22 r1 = 17/18/20/19 ms; cn4 = 17/57/16/17 ms. FE-side cost (audit Time minus engine span): cn1 q11.r1 951-733 = 218 ms, cn4 q11.r1 606-398 = 208 ms -> the FE fixed cost does NOT grow with CN count.
7. Impact overstated. Engine span cn1->cn4 (r1): q02 1066->1081 (1.0x), q22 770->697 (1.10x), q11 733->398 (1.84x), q15 4505->1819 (2.48x). For q02 and q22 the engine part itself does not scale, so the fixed cost is not 'the dominant reason' for their 1.08x/1.13x; it explains q11's 1.84x->1.46x only. Versus standalone, removing the entire pre-first-fragment cost still leaves cn1 at 2.2x (q11: (969-233)/336), 1.9x (q02), 1.6x (q22), 1.7x (q15): the majority of the standalone gap is inside the fragment span (inter-fragment gaps alone in cn1 q02.r1 sum to ~90 ms: 56d starts 14 ms after 569 finishes, 56c 18 ms after 56d, 566 15 ms after 567). The cost is also not constant: 118-262 ms across cn4 r1/r2 of these four queries.
8. Citation: engine.rs:1-14 describes a synchronous seam ('execute() blocks the caller'); the immediate-return behaviour is try_dispatch_sender/dispatch in compute_node_service.rs:305-336 (gated by SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1, set in capture-cn.sh:12), and dispatch_then_join (:351-377) keeps a sender RPC open until remote drains complete on multi-CN, so 'returns without waiting' is only true for local sender-only fragments.
9. Hygiene proposal (3): q02 references 5 tables (nation, part, partsupp, region, supplier) so it saves 3 RPCs, not 5-6 (q11 5, q15 6, q22 6). The expensive lineitem call is skipped for q02/q11/q22 either way.

Verdict: not refuted as a phenomenon (the ~200 ms pre-first-fragment cost, the 8 serial schema RPCs, and the level-by-level root-first deploy on the critical path are all confirmed), but the wave mechanism, the proposed FE change, the 4-CN number and the 'dominant reason' impact are contradicted or materially overstated by the code and the logs.
